steps.prompt: Only one word changes. How does the picture in your head change?
steps.a: The spider is on the box.
steps.b: The spider is in the box.
steps.reveal: “On” and “in” are prepositions: tiny words that show how one thing relates to another. Swap one and the whole scene (and how you feel about opening that box) changes.

cards.title: What prepositions do
cards.body: A preposition shows the relationship between a noun and another word: where something is (under the bed), when something happens (after lunch), or how (with a spoon). A preposition always has a noun or pronoun after it: its object.

cards.title: Prepositions of place
cards.text: in · on · under · over · above · below · behind · beside · next to · between · among · across · through · inside · outside · near · around · toward
cards.note: Between is for two (between Sam and Leo); among is for three or more (among the crowd).

cards.title: At, on, in for time
cards.text:
ON days and dates: on Monday, on May 4th
IN months, seasons, years, parts of the day: in July, in winter, in 2013, in the morning
AT clock times and night: at 3:15, at noon, at night
cards.note: Other time prepositions: before, after, during, since, until, for. Use “for” with an amount of time (for two hours) and “since” with a starting point (since Tuesday).

prompts: Which time preposition (at, on, in) is hardest for you to remember? Make up a trick to remember it.
Which preposition of place in your sentences gives the clearest picture?
